learning: Ten iterations show a sharp local optimum at the baseline. Lead, footprint, spread, track, radius, body length and mass each collapse or cut the oval when changed. The bend limit appears controller-side or deeper, and was not reachable by geometry in this search.
notes: Final package: the iteration-0 baseline geometry and controller, unchanged. This matches the Builder's final proposal and the design that reproduced 356.57 in iteration 9.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track race is scored on this design, so I deliver the proven baseline without speculative changes. Across ten races, the iteration-0 geometry is the only one that finishes any track. It finished 20/20 on the oval at about 1.65 s, and iteration 9 reproduced it exactly (score 356.57). Every other tested change either collapsed the oval or cut its finish rate, including the 0.7 kg mass test (iteration 10, 6/20, score 204). The controller is therefore kept exactly as the baseline that the platform was tuned against: kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2], last_direction. Changing gains now would be untested on any geometry and could break the one stable configuration. Sensor positions, footprint, drivetrain, mass and body are all baseline values. The bend failures (s-bend about 0.17 progress, slalom about 0.12) have not moved under any geometry tested, so I do not chase them here. The measurements requested cover completion, timing, error, line-loss and jitter, plus controller_errors and noise_robustness, so the race can be checked for exceptions and robustness.
